item.content:encoded: These two masterpieces are IMO the pièce de résistances of the PS2's legendary catalogue but more interestingly, are also technical marvels on the console. item.title: Meta introduces new memory compression CRSM on Linux with up to 452x speedup (5.4x in worst case scenario) compared to ZRAM (could help Linux gaming)
item.author: invalid@example.com (dex3108)
item.dc:creator: dex3108
item.content:encoded: A new compression model, called CRAM, offers a different path to compression that avoids swap entirely by keeping the compressed data in memory, and it offers up to 452x the performance of ZRAM. I was a kid in the 1990s when the idea seemed so simple to me: I can use PKZIP to compress my files, so why can't we do that with RAM? Indeed, I am not a singular genius, and many other people had the same idea, so memory compression has been a feature of most operating systems for a long... Click to expand... Click to shrink... item.title: Anyone have to game while recovering with their arm in a sling ?
item.author: invalid@example.com (Chaos Legion)
item.dc:creator: Chaos Legion
item.content:encoded: I'm getting surgery to fix a torn labrum in my shoulder in December. I figure I will have my arm in a sling for about 6 weeks, and then have a few months of physical therapy before I can really get back to my usual activities. So I'm looking make a dent on my backlog during this time. Given I'll only be able to use one hand for a while, I think it'll just have to be turn based JRPGs. Wanted to know if anyone had gone through a similar situation and any potential tips you had. Thanks in advance!
